questions.question: Which planet is commonly known as the Red Planet?
questions.explanation: Mars looks red because iron minerals in its soil oxidise, or rust.
questions.crispyBit1: Mars has two small moons: Phobos and Deimos.
questions.crispyBit2: A Martian day is about 24 hours and 37 minutes long.
questions.whoaFact: Olympus Mons on Mars is the largest known volcano in the solar system.

questions.question: In computing, what does CPU stand for?
questions.explanation: The CPU is the primary processor that executes instructions in a computer.
questions.crispyBit1: Modern CPUs can contain multiple processing cores.
questions.crispyBit2: A CPU’s clock speed is commonly measured in gigahertz.
questions.whoaFact: A modern processor can perform billions of clock cycles every second.

questions.question: Which animal has three hearts?
questions.explanation: An octopus has one systemic heart and two branchial hearts that pump blood through its gills.
questions.crispyBit1: Octopus blood is blue because it uses copper-rich haemocyanin.
questions.crispyBit2: Most of an octopus’s neurons are located in its arms.
questions.whoaFact: An octopus can taste using receptors in its suckers.

questions.question: Which conflict is commonly described as history’s shortest war?
questions.explanation: The Anglo-Zanzibar War of 1896 ended in less than an hour.
questions.crispyBit1: The conflict began on the morning of 27 August 1896.
questions.crispyBit2: Its duration is usually given as roughly 38 to 45 minutes.
questions.whoaFact: It was over before many modern feature films would reach their halfway point.

questions.question: What does the forensic term rigor mortis describe?
questions.explanation: Rigor mortis is the post-mortem stiffening of muscles caused by chemical changes in muscle tissue.
questions.crispyBit1: Rigor mortis is one of several post-mortem changes used in forensic assessment.
questions.crispyBit2: Temperature and physical conditions can affect how quickly it develops.
questions.whoaFact: It is never used alone to determine an exact time of death.
questions.sourceName: NCBI Bookshelf — Evaluation of Postmortem Changes
